title: Performance Benchmarking Lab reference solution
explanation: A checksum keeps the result observable and a warm-up reduces—but does not eliminate—JIT effects. Treat this as a measurement exercise, not a reliable microbenchmark; use JMH for publishable comparisons.

hidden_tests.input_or_setup: Use the deterministic sample data or representative valid input described in the exercise.
hidden_tests.expected_behavior: Prints a deterministic checksum and a machine-dependent elapsed time
hidden_tests.purpose: Verify the main behavior and the output contract.

hidden_tests.input_or_setup: Test empty, zero, minimum/maximum, duplicate, or end-of-range input as appropriate to the exercise.
hidden_tests.expected_behavior: The result matches the documented boundary rule and does not silently corrupt state.

hidden_tests.input_or_setup: Provide malformed input or simulate a missing file, unavailable endpoint, missing configuration, or database failure where relevant.
hidden_tests.expected_behavior: The operation fails clearly or returns a safe result; resources are released and secrets are not printed.
hidden_tests.purpose: Check explicit error behavior and cleanup.

review_notes: Repository-only reference material. Keep it out of public API responses and frontend bundles. The platform grader is only a required-token smoke check; complete task-specific execution tests in an isolated Java runner before publication.
sample_expected_result: Prints a deterministic checksum and a machine-dependent elapsed time
